entityDescription:
Istituto Superiore per la Protezione e la Ricerca Ambientale (ISPRA, eng: Italian Institute for Environmental Protection and Research), has been established by Legislative Decree no. 112 of 25 June 2008, converted into Law no. 133 (with amendments) on 21 August 2008. is a Public research body acting under the vigilance of the Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security, and provided with technical, scientific, organizational, managerial, administrative and financial autonomy. ISPRA performs scientific and technological research applied to environmental protection as well as assessment, monitoring, control, communication, training and education activities. The main activities are related to environmental characterization, monitoring and reporting with respect to prevention, evaluation and mitigation of impacts, quality of the environment, habitats and biodiversity; stainable use of resources.
ISPRA coordinates the National System of Environment Protection Agencies (SNPA -21 environmental agencies of the Italian regions and autonomous provinces), ensuring the exchange of information and expertise on environmental monitoring, control and inspections, connecting scientific knowledge communities with environmental administrators and policy makers at national and local level.
ISPRA performs the function of the Geological Service of Italy, of National Focal Point of EEA/EIONET and of UNEP/MAP INFO-RAC.
ISPRA experts are fully engaged, in support of the Italian Ministry of the Environment, in several technical working groups for the implementation of EU directives and regulations (e.g. Habitats, Birds, Invasive Alien Species, Water, MSFD, INSPIRE, Air Quality, Waste, REACH and others).

entityDescription: The Consorzio Futuro in Ricerca (CFR) was established in 1993. It is a private non-profit organization, with public and private participation, aimed at the promotion, development and enhancement of human, scientific, technological and economic resources .The CFR promotes and manages research and innovation through projects carried out in collaboration with universities, research centres, public entities, industrial companies, in Italy and abroad, as well as linking know-how generators, industrial organizations and the working world.CFR chiefly activates in the field of precompetitive research and technological transfer for industrial application. Its activity is complementary to the institutional actions taken by the University of Ferrara, member of the consortium, evaluating its technical-scientific and human competences.The institutional activities assumed by CFR consist in the conclusion and technical-administrative management of research contracts, the coordination of scientific manifestations, and the organisation of educational events on behalf of public and private companies on a local, national or international scale.During its more than twenty years of business, the CFR has received orders with more than 800 national and international public and private buyers, subscribing to more than 5000 contracts for a total value of over 145 million Euros.CFR is committed to promoting and activating research contracts and agreements with companies, industry, small and medium-sized businesses and public administration regarding the following areas: protection of the environment, food technologies and biotechnology; architectural innovation, urban economics, and restoration technology; technology of polymers and innovative materials; innovations in engineering, data processing, electronic, energetic, pharmaceutical, physical, chemical, mathematical, geological, mineralogical and biological technologies; linguistic innovations, musical and multimedia technologies; economic, juridical, and organisational analysis.CFR provides information on current research programmes run by the laboratories of the members of the consortium, it provides information and support for the realisation of tests, analysis and certification at the laboratories of members of the consortium or of third parties, it provides support to draft contracts and agreements with public or private institutions, support for the organisation and management and/or immediate organisation and management of Master courses, courses of further education, of vocational retraining and professional further training, also by means of specific scholarships, doctoral research scholarships and post-doctoral scholarships.CFR provides support to the companies in terms of advanced technologies by offering advice and services; it creates and/or participates in auxiliary societies which may also be profit societies in order to carry out certain activities (organisation of conferences, technical-administrative spin-off management, etc.); it promotes cooperation agreements also on an international scale between research institutions and industrial companies.CFR takes care of coordinating all the activities involved in the participation and management of the various types of intervention, from the administrative part to the entire organisation of the project itself. In particular, it not only takes care to identify the opportunities of participation at the various financing programmes, but it is also committed to: communicating the information gathered; preparing the required documentation and finally forwarding it to the determined institutional organs; writing the necessary press coverage.In order to promote and evaluate research results and in order to develop scientific and business culture CFR plans and organizes events on a national and international scale.

entityDescription:
University of Eastern Finland
The University of Eastern Finland is the most multidisciplinary university in Finland. Our high standard of interdisciplinary research and education respond to global challenges and build a sustainable future. Our research is ranked among the best in the world in several fields. We offer education in nearly 100 major subjects and we train experts for tomorrow’s changing labourmarket needs. 

The University of Eastern Finland was established in 2010, following a decision by the University of Joensuu (est. 1969) and the University of Kuopio (est. 1972) to join forces in a merger. TRANSVALOR S.A. was created in 1984 to transfer to the industry and valorise the research results of the Mines ParisTech science labs. Transvalor´s main shareholder is ARMINES.
Initially, Transvalor specialized as a scientific software editor and obtained an international commercial success with software in the material forming simulation domain. In early 2009, Transvalor created Transvalor Innovation, a department to promote further the transfer and valorisation activity for all the research labs of MINES ParisTech. One dedicated 5-person team (of which three are doctors) in Transvalor Innovation is working with the O.I.E. (Observation Impacts Energy - http://www.oie.mines-paristech.fr) MINES ParisTech research lab on the industrialisation, valorisation and commercialisation of the HelioClim solar irradiation databases, the SoDa web site and all type of value added activity in the solar resource domain.
Today, the SoDa web site (www.soda-pro.com) registers more than 76 000 unique visitors per year. Over 135 millions of requests of irradiation data through WGET service were fulfilled in 2018. The SoDa web site hosts also the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) solar radiation products access.
Transvalor Innovation has participated and continues to participate to several R&D programs with the Mines ParisTech-ARMINES/O.I.E centre and/or the DLR. Within these R&D programs, its main role is to integrate products as web services (WFS and WPS) or as value added services, to build and maintain the hardware/software infrastructure needed to operate these services and to disseminate/distribute these services to a large panel of customers/stakeholders.
More than 70 customers have an annual subscription service with Transvalor to obtain solar irradiation data from the SoDa web site. In the recent years, we have delivered various services and/or data to several hundreds of different companies.
